newsitem.title: USA: Rhode Island leading indicator index up in Q3.
newsitem.headline: Rhode Island leading indicator index up in Q3.

text.p: The University of Rhode Island/Providence Journal index of leading economic indicators was up 0.26 percent in the third quarter of 1996 - the third consecutive quarterly increase, the Providence Journal reported Tuesday.
The Rhode Island index, which includes nine local and national indicators, predicts whether the economy will expand or contract in the near term.

"The implication is that the Rhode Island economy will continue to grow in 1997," University of Rhode Island economics professor Glenworth Ramsay, model manager of the Rhode Island index told the newspaper. "But the growth is slowing down. That's a warning sign for later on in 1997."

Still Ramsay told the newspaper the overall index number of 105.17, the highest level since the third quarter of 1995, is good news, particularly following a recent strong report on consumer confidence in Rhode Island.

Rhode Island's seasonally adjusted unemployment rate for September was 5.1 percent -- a full two percentage points below what it was in September 1995. There were 18,3000 more Rhode Islanders holding jobs in September than a year earlier, the newspaper reported.
